plan: Eliminate all leveraged ETFs to reduce risk.
Sell remaining leveraged semiconductor and AI/Software ETFs.

conservative.read: This mode prioritizes capital preservation with a target of ~1.5% monthly return. It significantly reduces leverage and focuses on less volatile assets, aiming for low drawdowns. Risk is minimized by cutting all leveraged ETFs and reducing concentration.

plan: Reduce exposure in leveraged ETFs to manage risk.
Trim positions in MUU, METU, PLTU, and MSFU.
Add CRCL, a top-rated long setup.
This plan balances growth with risk management.
It aims for steady growth with controlled drawdowns.
Leverage is kept at a manageable level.
balanced.read: This balanced approach targets ~2.5% monthly return by blending broad market exposure with quality tech and controlled leverage. Risk is managed by trimming leveraged ETFs and adding a high-potential new name. Drawdowns are expected to be moderate.

plan: Increase exposure in leveraged ETFs for aggressive growth.
Add to SOXL, SPAL, MUU, METU, PLTU, and MSFU.
Initiate a new position in CRCL with significant allocation.
This plan aims for maximum growth potential.
It embraces higher concentration and leverage.
Expect significantly higher potential upside and downside.
aggressive.read: This aggressive mode targets ~4% monthly return by maximizing leverage and concentration in high-scoring setups, including leveraged ETFs. It accepts substantially higher potential drawdowns and the risk of leveraged ETF decay. Strict stop discipline is critical to manage risk.

plan: Eliminate all leveraged ETFs to prioritize income.
Sell remaining leveraged semiconductor and AI/Software ETFs.
Increase allocation to QQQI for income generation.
This plan focuses on steady monthly distributions.
It aims for low drawdowns and reliable income.
Growth potential is secondary to income stability.
income.read: This income-focused mode targets ~1% monthly return by prioritizing income-generating assets like QQQI and cutting all high-beta, leveraged positions. It aims for low drawdowns and consistent distributions, treating the portfolio more like a yield-generating instrument. NAV can still fall in market downturns.
